newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, LME stock hike expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, LME stock hike expected.

text.p: COMEX copper settled lower on disappointment with LME's failure to break through upside resistance and expectations of a sizeable hike in the London exchange's stocks on Friday, traders said.
LME three months price met resistance in its bid to break through $2,300 per tonne, prompting some profit-taking by speculators, said Fred Demler of E D and F Man International.
"There is also a call for copper stocks to be up 5,000 to 8,000 tonnes, largely in the U.S., but maybe a little bit also in Singapore and West Europe," Demler said.

Spot LME is trading at a premium over its COMEX counterpart, and the New York exchange's copper stocks have fallen sharply this week, down 6,091 short tons Monday through Wednesday, metal which is expected to show up in LME warehouses.
March COMEX settled 1.10 cents weaker at 105.80 cents per pound, traded 108.00 to 105.25 cents. Spot January went out 0.90 cent lower at 108.50 cents.
The LME backwardation, which traders said is supporting the market, also eased some $5 to $10 Thursday to $171/$180.
